title: Arrests and Trials

columns.name: Special Laws & Local Acts | Below 16 years

notes: 12.2.6 Age-group distribution of arrested persons for IPC & SLL crimes (both) reveal similar pattern during the last three years. However, it is noted that share of arrestees in the age-groups 18-30 years for IPC crimes increased marginally from 51 to 52 while share under age group 30-50 years decreased marginally from 39.4 to 37.9.

12.2.7 Table-70 gives information on persons arrested on an average per case under IPC and SLL for the years 1993 to 1997. It is seen that arrests made per case in 1997 is almost the same as in 1996 for IPC cases. In Violent crimes such as Murder, Attempt to commit Murder, Culpable Homicide not amounting to Murder, Dowry Death and Cruelty by Husband or Relatives, an average 2 persons per case were arrested signifying the accomplice involvement in such cases. Similarly, in SLL cases, such as those relating to Gambling Act, Protection of Civil Rights Act, Dowry Prohibition Act, on an average 2 persons were taken into custody by Police. The higher arrests per case in cases of Preparation & Assembly for Dacoity (4.7), Riots (5.0) and Independent Representation of Women (P) Act (3.8) were specific to the nature of such crimes perpetrated by a group or gangs.
Disposal of persons arrested under the IPC crimes by Police

12.3.1 During the year, a total of 32,03,284 persons were either under custody or on bail for 21,95,848 various IPC offences under investigation by Police. These also include persons in whose cases the investigations remained pending at the end of year 1996.
